lines: Cracks spread if ignored. You noticed this one. Now prove you can patch it.
Mortar takes time to set. So does forgiveness.
You made a crack. You named it. That's the first proper repair.
Don't plaster over this and call it fixed.
Fine. A foundation can be reset, but it takes honest work.
I hear the apology. Now bring mortar, not dust.
Damage hidden inside stone still spreads. Keep this in the open.
Trust can stand again if the base is not shaken twice.
You owned what you did. That counts for something.
I would rather hear an awkward truth than a polished excuse.
That helps, though it does not undo the damage.
We can work forward from here if you keep your word.
I am not asking you to grovel. I am asking you to do better.
Tell the others you were wrong too, not only me.
I can forgive a mistake more easily than a lie about it.
Your apology sounds real. Let your next choice match it.
I do not want another speech. Help with the repair instead.
We are not square yet, but at least we are facing the same problem.
I will stop carrying the anger when I see the habit change.
Alright. Let us see whether this repair lasts.
